observation_summary: The BisectionSolver.solve(f, min, max, initial) method throws a NullPointerException because it incorrectly delegates to the solve(min, max) method instead of the solve(f, min, max) method, causing the solver to attempt to use an uninitialized function member variable.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic interface mismatch where the implementation of one method (the 4-parameter solve) incorrectly calls a different method (the 2-parameter solve) that relies on a state variable (the function 'f') which is not set in the context of the 4-parameter call. This is a communication/contract error between the internal methods of the class.
evidence_used: Bug report description: 'BisectionSolver.solve(final UnivariateRealFunction f, double min, double max, double initial) invokes BisectionSolver.solve(double min, double max) which throws NullPointerException, as member variable UnivariateRealSolverImpl.f is null. Instead the method: BisectionSolver.solve(final UnivariateRealFunction f, double min, double max) should be called.'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the logic is technically a method call, the root cause is the incorrect selection of an interface/method signature that leads to a contract violation (using an uninitialized member variable).
